# Dynamical Lie algebras (quantum) and bracket-generating / growth-vector notions (classical control) as homes for "depth-graded dimension of the Lie algebra generated by pairwise Hamiltonians"

**Method note / caveat.** Web search worked, but direct full-text fetching of arxiv.org, ar5iv, nature.com, quantum-journal.org, PMC, pennylane docs, readthedocs, aimsciences, semanticscholar and several mirrors was blocked by this session's network allowlist. Every finding below therefore rests on abstracts, publisher landing pages, and search-returned excerpts, not on a reading of full papers. Where I could not verify a detail (in particular: tables of depth-graded dimensions inside a paper), I say so and list it as a gap rather than guessing. Research date: 2026-11-08.

**One-line summary for the researcher.** The object "Lie algebra generated by a set of Hamiltonians, graded by bracket length / nesting depth, with its dimension sequence" has two named homes: (a) in quantum variational circuits it is the *dynamical Lie algebra* (DLA), but that literature almost always reports only the dimension of the *closed* algebra, not the depth filtration; (b) in classical geometric control it is the *growth vector* of a bracket-generating distribution (finite-dimensional, pointwise), and, closest of all, the **McLachlan–Ryland / McLachlan–Murua "Lie algebra of classical mechanics"** program, which computes exactly a graded dimension sequence of the Poisson algebra generated by kinetic and potential energy and compares it to the free Lie algebra (Witt) counts. No source found computes the depth-graded dimension sequence for *pairwise* interaction Hamiltonians of an N-body system; that specific object appears to be unreported.

---

## Key question 1 — Quantum DLA literature (Larocca et al. 2022; Ragone et al. 2024; Wiersema et al. 2024; Kökcü et al. 2024; Aguilar et al. 2024): what is computed, final dimension vs depth filtration, free-Lie-algebra bounds?

### Takeaway
All of these works define the DLA as the real span of the Lie closure (all nested commutators) of a generator set and report the *dimension of the closed algebra* (and its scaling with qubit number n, polynomial vs exponential) as the diagnostic for barren plateaus / classical simulability. None of the abstracts, landing pages or excerpts I could access reports the dimension as a function of nesting depth (a filtration), and none mentions free-Lie-algebra (Witt/Hall-basis) upper bounds; the depth-graded sequence does appear implicitly only as the iteration count of numerical closure algorithms (PennyLane `lie_closure`, `fastdla`), where "iteration" = nesting depth.

### Cited Findings
- Larocca, Ju, García-Martín, Coles, Cerezo, "Diagnosing barren plateaus with tools from quantum optimal control": "the work establishes a link between the existence of barren plateaus and the scaling of the dimension of g" where g is the DLA, "the subspace of operator space spanned by the nested commutators of the ansatz generators"; results also depend on the input state; QAOA and HVA are analysed and no-go results for controllable systems (spin glasses) are given — [arXiv:2105.14377](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.14377v3); [Macquarie listing](https://researchers.mq.edu.au/en/publications/diagnosing-barren-plateaus-with-tools-from-quantum-optimal-contro/). The search returned nothing defining a nesting-depth filtration in this paper; only dim(g) of the closed algebra is discussed in the accessible text.
- A related statement of the DLA definition: "the real span of the Lie closure (i.e., closure under taking commutators) of the generators" — [Diaz, García-Martín, Kazi, Larocca, Cerezo, "Showcasing a barren plateau theory beyond the DLA"](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2310.11505).
- Ragone et al., "A Lie algebraic theory of barren plateaus for deep parameterized quantum circuits" (Nat. Commun. 2024; arXiv:2309.09342): "for a 2-design of the dynamical Lie group, gradient variance scales inversely with the dimension of the DLA" (search excerpt); the theory requires "initial states or observables that lie in the circuit's Lie algebra" — [arXiv:2309.09342](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.09342); companion paper [Fontana et al., Nat. Commun. 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-49910-w.pdf). No depth-filtration dimension appears in the accessible abstract.
- Wiersema, Kökcü, Kemper, Bakalov, "Classification of dynamical Lie algebras for translation-invariant 2-local spin systems in one dimension" (npj Quantum Inf. 10, 110 (2024); arXiv:2309.05690): "We consider chains with open and periodic boundary conditions and find 17 unique dynamical Lie algebras"; also treats "systems with a fully connected topology"; recovers transverse-field Ising and Heisenberg plus "more exotic classes of Hamiltonians that cannot be identified easily" — [arXiv:2309.05690](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2309.05690); [npj QI listing](https://doaj.org/article/1d01bd343fb54e118b4477fa1d805f1d); [PMC copy](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11540907). The result is a classification of *closed* algebras (which Lie algebra, e.g. so(2n), su(2^n), and their dimension scaling), not a depth sequence.
- Kökcü, Wiersema, Kemper, Bakalov, "Classification of dynamical Lie algebras generated by spin interactions on undirected graphs" (arXiv:2409.19797, Sept 2024; listed as J. Math. Phys. 67(5), 2026, DOI 10.1063/5.0283277): "the one-dimensional case is special; for any other graph, the dynamical Lie algebra solely depends on whether the graph is bipartite or not"; "Non-trivial polynomially scaling DLAs appear only on 1D line or circle topologies, and all other DLAs have dimensions scaling exponentially with the system size" — [arXiv:2409.19797](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.19797); [Kemper lab page](https://kemperlab.github.io/papers/Kokcu-classification/). Again a closed-algebra classification; the "interaction graph" of pairwise couplings is the organising datum, which is the nearest quantum analogue of "a set of two-body interaction Hamiltonians on N particles".
- Aguilar et al., "Full classification of Pauli Lie algebras" (arXiv:2408.00081): I could not access the abstract or text (fetch blocked, and searches did not return excerpts). Listed as a gap below.
- "On the dynamical Lie algebras of quantum approximate optimization algorithms" (Quantum, 2026): DLA dimension for QAOA-type circuits "scales as O(n³)" with "an explicit basis", plus "upper bounds on the dimension of QAOA-MaxCut DLAs for arbitrary graphs, and on the dimension of their centers" — [Quantum](https://quantum-journal.org/papers/q-2026-05-29-2119/pdf/). Bounds are on the closed algebra, not depth-graded.
- "Expressivity limits in quantum walk-based optimization" derives "new upper bounds on DLA dimension" for QWOA — [arXiv:2508.05749](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.05749). Closed-algebra bounds.
- A QTML abstract ("Dynamical Lie algebra and CNOT gates") claims "after a finite number of layers the maximal DLA is reached" with "an upper bound on the number of layers tied to the order of a certain element, using the Pauli group over F₂" — [indico abstract](https://indico.nithecs.ac.za/event/12/contributions/476/attachments/349/385/abstract_QTML_CNOT_all.pdf). This is the only quantum item found that bounds a *depth* at which closure occurs; it concerns circuit layers, not an explicit dimension-per-depth sequence, and I could not verify its statement.
- A 2026 preprint "Dynamical Lie Algebras Cannot Describe Shallow QAOA: Cragged Terrains, Barren Plateaus, and Empirical Hardness Models" argues the closed-DLA picture fails for shallow circuits — [arXiv:2608.04252](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.04252). (Relevant because it is precisely the gap between "closed algebra" and "finite nesting depth" that your filtration measures; details unverified.)
- Numerical closure tooling makes the depth filtration visible as a by-product: PennyLane `qml.lie_closure` documents `max_iterations (int): maximum depth of nested commutators to consider. Default is 10000`, and `verbose (bool): whether to print out progress updates`; in the stable source "each loop pass prints the epoch number and the current DLA size", whereas the latest source prints only a final summary — [PennyLane docs](https://docs.pennylane.ai/en/stable/code/api/pennylane.lie_closure.html); [source](https://docs.pennylane.ai/en/stable/_modules/pennylane/liealg/lie_closure.html). Iiyama, "Fast numerical generation of Lie closure" (arXiv:2506.01120, June 2025) addresses the cost of the linear-independence test that "practically limited [closure] to trivially small matrix sizes" and proposes two alternatives; implemented in the `fastdla` library — [arXiv:2506.01120](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.01120); [fastdla docs](https://fastdla.readthedocs.io/en/stable/apidocs/lie_closure.html).
- Free-Lie-algebra tools (Hall basis, Witt formula) appear in the quantum literature only in the context of commutator-free Magnus/time-propagation, where the Hall basis is "the standard tool for the free Lie algebra ... because the Jacobi identity and antisymmetry make raw nested commutators linearly dependent" — [Alvermann & Fehske, arXiv:1102.5071](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5071). No DLA paper found invokes Witt bounds.
- Historical quantum many-body precedent (not DLA-named): Albertini & D'Alessandro, "The Lie algebra structure and nonlinear controllability of spin systems" derive necessary and sufficient controllability conditions for networks of interacting spin-1/2 from the Lie algebra generated by the Hamiltonian, linked to connectedness of an interaction graph — [arXiv:quant-ph/0106115](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0106115v2). Dodd–Nielsen–Bremner–Thew: "any desired two-body Hamiltonian evolution" can be simulated "using any fixed two-body entangling n-qubit Hamiltonian and local unitaries" — [arXiv:quant-ph/0106064](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0106064). Bremner et al.: an "odd" Hamiltonian with local unitaries generates so(2^n) or sp(2^n) rather than su(2^n) — [arXiv:quant-ph/0307148](https://web3.arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0307148). A recent "Universal computation with magic Hamiltonians" counts Pauli strings to get dimensions such as 2n²−n for so(2n) — [arXiv:2609.14757](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.14757). All report closed-algebra identity/dimension only.

### Inferences
- The quantum DLA community has the right *object* (Lie closure of a generator set of 2-local terms) but, in everything accessible here, uses only the *terminal* invariant dim(g). Your per-depth sequence would be a refinement they do not tabulate; the natural place it already lives is the epoch counter of `lie_closure`-type algorithms.
- The quantum setting differs structurally: Pauli-string DLAs are finite-dimensional (≤ 4^n − 1) so the filtration must stabilise; your classical polynomial Poisson algebra is infinite-dimensional, so the depth sequence is the primary invariant rather than a transient. The analogy is therefore "analogous in definition, different in asymptotics" — the quantum works should be cited as the named precedent for the construction, not for the growth phenomenon.

### Gaps
- Could not read Larocca et al., Ragone et al., Wiersema et al., Kökcü et al. in full; cannot rule out that an appendix tabulates DLA size per closure iteration (e.g. for numerical examples). Queries tried: "dynamical Lie algebra nested commutator depth dimension growth barren plateaus"; "Larocca ... 'depth'"; "'dynamical Lie algebra' 'free Lie algebra' OR 'Hall basis' OR 'Witt' ... depth". None surfaced a depth-graded table.
- Aguilar et al. "Full classification of Pauli Lie algebras" (arXiv:2408.00081): fetch blocked, no search excerpts obtained. Unverified.
- Whether any DLA paper explicitly compares dim(g) to free-Lie-algebra (Witt) bounds: no evidence found (negative result after the query above).

## Key question 2 — Classical geometric control: Lie algebra rank condition, bracket-generating distributions, growth vectors, nilpotent approximations; Hamiltonian / N-body controllability via pairwise interactions

### Takeaway
The *growth vector* of a bracket-generating distribution is precisely a dimension sequence indexed by bracket depth and is a standard named invariant (Chow–Rashevskii, equiregularity, nilpotent approximation), but it is pointwise and bounded by dim M, so it is only analogous to an infinite-dimensional Poisson-algebra filtration. Classical controllability of chains of particles with pairwise potentials has been studied (Sarychev 2009) via Lie-bracket/accessibility arguments, and Lewis treats "mechanical systems with Hamiltonian control vector fields", but I found no paper that reports a bracket-depth dimension sequence for Hamiltonian vector fields of pairwise interactions.

### Cited Findings
- Bracket-generating and Chow–Rashevskii: a family of vector fields is bracket generating if "Lie(L)(x) equals the tangent space at every point"; then "every two points can be joined by a trajectory" — [Agrachev lecture notes (SISSA)](https://people.sissa.it/~agrachev/agrachev_files/rome06.pdf); [Simić, tutorial on geometric control](https://softbank.iust.ac.ir/MathBooks/S/Simic%20-%20A%20Tutorial%20on%20geometric%20control%20theory,%202000..PDF); [MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Bracket-GeneratingDistribution.html).
- Growth vector: "The dimensions of these successive spaces form the growth vector. If all these dimensions are constant on the manifold, the distribution is equiregular"; for rank k the maximal (generic/free) growth is "(k, k(k+1)/2, …)" — [Distributions and controllability problems (II), arXiv:2401.07560](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.07560); [EMS Press article](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/17078).
- Free nilpotent Lie algebras realise the maximal growth vector: for two generators the cumulative dimensions run "2, 3, 5, 8, 14, 23, 41, 71, ..." with graded dimensions given by a Witt-type recursion i·l_d(i) = d^i − Σ j·l_d(j) — [Sachkov, "On Carnot algebra with growth vector (2,3,5,8)", arXiv:1304.1035](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1304.1035); [Diophantine properties of nilpotent Lie groups, arXiv:1307.1489](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1307.1489). (The cumulative sequence here is exactly a "dimension of the depth filtration" sequence, so the growth vector is the named classical analogue of your 3, 6, 17, 116 — but in a free nilpotent model, not for Hamiltonian fields.)
- Applied growth-vector computation for a mechanism: Hrdina & Zalabová, "Local geometric control of a certain mechanism with the growth vector (4,7)" (J. Dyn. Control Syst. 2020) compute the filtration from control fields and their brackets, note the one-link version has growth vector (3,6), and study the nilpotent approximation as a control problem on a Lie group — [MUNI record](https://is.muni.cz/publication/1694536/cs?zoomy_is=1).
- Hamiltonian controls in mechanics: Lewis (Queen's, 1995) "proposes a new controllability definition" for mechanical systems and "studies systems whose control vector fields are Hamiltonian and obtains decompositions describing the controllable and uncontrollable dynamics" — [Lewis preprint](https://mast.queensu.ca/~andrew/papers/pdf/1995e.pdf). Manikonda et al. treat controlled Hamiltonian systems on T*G via Lie–Poisson reduction and a Lie algebra rank condition — [Manikonda et al.](https://robotics.umd.edu/%7Ekrishna/images/manikonda_psk.pdf).
- The correspondence used throughout: Lie bracket of Hamiltonian vector fields corresponds to the Poisson bracket of Hamiltonians, "{H_A, H_B} = H_[A,B]" for quadratic Hamiltonians / linear fields — [Jakubczyk slides 2011](https://folk.ntnu.no/kurusche/Slides/SanDiegoRPCCT2011_Jakubczyk.pdf); [controllability of induced bilinear systems on the sphere, arXiv:2506.07749](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.07749).
- Thermodynamic/contact analogue: a paper on the geometry of thermodynamic processes "uses the Poisson algebra generated by the Hamiltonians to analyze local accessibility", defining an accessibility algebra spanned by contact vector fields built from that Poisson algebra — [arXiv:1811.04227](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1811.04227).
- Classical N-body chain with pairwise potentials: Sarychev, "Controlling multiparticle system on a line. I" (J. Differential Equations 2009; arXiv:0809.2365) studies n particles on a line where "only neighboring particles interact through a Hamiltonian with a pairwise potential", proves accessibility for any T>0 with "a single control (force), applied to either P1 or Pn" (Theorem 2.2) via "Lie-bracket distributions along zero-time orbits" (Lemma 2.2); for forcing an intermediate particle, "for a generic φ the Lie rank is complete ... Still for special choice of φ the system may possess low-dimensional orbits" — [arXiv:0809.2365](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0809.2365); [IDEAS listing](https://ideas.repec.org/p/flo/wpaper/2008-01.html). Part II (periodic case): "global controllability by means of single controlling force of the multiparticle system with a generic potential of interaction" — [arXiv:0812.0997](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.0997).
- Agrachev, Kazandjian, Pozzoli (2025) study "small-time controllability ... on the Lie groups SL2(R) and SL2(R)⋉[Heisenberg]" for classical and quantum harmonic oscillators, using "good Lie brackets" — [SISSA preprint](https://people.sissa.it/~agrachev/agrachev_files/oscil.pdf). Finite-dimensional (quadratic Hamiltonians) only.
- Agrachev, Baryshnikov, Sarychev (ESAIM COCV 2016): ensemble controllability treated by viewing "the ensemble as a single system on a cartesian product of N copies of the state space M" and applying Lie rank methods — [arXiv:1603.07133](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/1603.07133).
- A different "control of n bodies" paper builds finite-dimensional control vector fields for n particles on R and S¹ with separation constraints, with controllability tied to Lie brackets spanning the tangent space — [arXiv:2209.10824](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.10824).
- Degree bookkeeping for polynomial vector fields: Chyba et al. note that for mechanical systems with polynomial forces "the degrees of Lie brackets of polynomial vector fields can be bounded" — [arXiv:math/0205017](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0205017).

### Inferences
- "Growth vector" is the accepted classical name for "dimension of the bracket-depth filtration"; your depth-filtration numbers (3, 6, 17, 116) are formally a growth-vector-like sequence of an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra of Hamiltonian functions, not of a distribution on a finite-dimensional manifold. Calling it "the growth vector of the Poisson algebra generated by the pair Hamiltonians" would be understood but should be flagged as an extension of the term (the distribution spanned by the Hamiltonian vector fields on a 2·3d-dimensional phase space has a bona fide growth vector that saturates at ≤ 6d; the function algebra does not).
- Sarychev's chain-of-particles papers are the closest classical N-body controllability precedent (pairwise potential, Lie-rank/accessibility), but they fix the interaction and switch external forces, whereas your setting switches *which pairwise interaction is on*. No paper was found for the latter in classical mechanics; the quantum analogue (switching 2-local couplings on an interaction graph) is Albertini–D'Alessandro and Kökcü et al.

### Gaps
- No source found for "growth vector of Hamiltonian vector fields of pairwise interactions" or "Lie algebra generated by {T_i + T_j + V(q_i − q_j)}" in classical control. Queries tried: "growth vector distribution bracket generating Hamiltonian vector fields controllability"; "'growth vector' Hamiltonian system controllability Poisson bracket filtration mechanical system"; "controllability N-body Hamiltonian system switching pairwise interactions Lie algebra rank condition"; "classical N-body controllability 'pairwise' coupling control Hamiltonian particles Poisson bracket 'Lie algebra' infinite-dimensional". All negative for the specific object.
- Agrachev–Sachkov, Jurdjevic, Bloch, d'Alessandro textbooks: not accessible here; I cannot confirm whether any contains a worked Poisson-algebra growth computation for interacting particles. Textbook-level content on LARC and growth vectors is assumed standard (see Agrachev notes / Simić tutorial above).

## Key question 3 — Is there literature computing the Lie algebra generated by pairwise Hamiltonians {p_i²/2 + p_j²/2 + V(q_i − q_j)} (or similar) as polynomial/rational functions, reporting infinite dimensionality with depth-wise dimensions?

### Takeaway
The closest match — and the one most likely to be the "named home" — is the McLachlan–Ryland (2003) / McLachlan–Murua (2019) "Lie algebra of classical mechanics": the Lie algebra generated by kinetic energy T and potential V under the canonical Poisson bracket, graded by word length (and by momentum degree), whose homogeneous dimensions c_n are computed and whose growth rate ("algebraic entropy") lim c_n^{1/n} = 1.8249… is reported, with explicit identities such as {V,{V,{V,T}}} = 0 showing the algebra is strictly smaller than the free Lie algebra on two generators (Witt counts). No source was found doing this for a *set of pairwise* Hamiltonians on N particles.

### Cited Findings
- McLachlan & Ryland, "The algebraic entropy of classical mechanics" (J. Math. Phys. 44, 2003; arXiv:math-ph/0210030): introduces the Lie algebra generated by kinetic and potential energy under the canonical Poisson bracket; "the homogeneous dimensions of the free Lie algebra follow Witt's formula"; for simple mechanical systems "the order conditions for the bracket {V,{V,{V,T}}} and all its higher brackets can be dropped"; "the Lie algebra is never free, regardless of T, V, or the dimension of the system"; the paper "introduces a class of Lie algebras graded by degree in the momentum variable", noting this grading "is quite different from the natural grading of a free Lie algebra"; reported entropy 1.82542377420108, described as "a fundamental constant associated to classical mechanics" — [arXiv:math-ph/0210030](https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0210030); [AIP](https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.1576904). The abstract is also explicit that "General splitting methods instead need one condition for each dimension of the degree-n piece, counted by Witt's formula" — [arXiv PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math-ph/0210030).
- McLachlan & Murua, "The Lie algebra of classical mechanics" (J. Comput. Dyn. 2019; arXiv:1905.07554): the algebra "splits into an abelian part spanned by 'modified' potential energies, which is isomorphic to a free commutative nonassociative algebra on one generator, plus a free algebra generated by the kinetic energy and its bracket with that abelian part"; "Because kinetic energy is quadratic in the momenta, the algebra satisfies identities beyond skew-symmetry and Jacobi"; "some brackets vanish for every choice of energies, regardless of system dimension"; the authors "compute the dimensions c_n of the homogeneous subspaces and find the entropy limit c_n^(1/n) equals 1.8249…" (body value 1.82491116005236559371…); they "conjecture that systems with Euclidean kinetic energy metrics already give a free algebra" (i.e. no further identities); "at each order n there are dim L^n(A,B) such order conditions"; and they state the 2003 construction "is in error starting at order 13" — [arXiv:1905.07554](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.07554); [J. Comput. Dyn.](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/jcd.2019017); [Semantic Scholar](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/The-Lie-algebra-of-classical-mechanics-McLachlan-Murua/e4b6809dff9ccb215438692806c4f4d6de363957).
- Infinite-dimensional Vlasov–Poisson analogue: Casas, Crouseilles, Faou, Mehrenberger exploit the same nested bracket "[[[T,U],U],U] = 0" to reduce splitting order conditions to Runge–Kutta–Nyström form — [Casas et al. (HAL preprint)](https://www.i2m.univ-amu.fr/perso/mehrenberger.m/ccfm_splitvp_hal.pdf). A quantum-chemistry Trotter paper notes "[V,[V,[V,T]]] = 0 fails in a truncated plane-wave basis", i.e. the identity holds in the continuum but not after discretisation — [arXiv:2606.30741](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.30741).
- Munthe-Kaas & Owren, "Computations in a free Lie algebra" (Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 357, 1999): "Witt's formula for counting commutators in a free Lie algebra is generalized to the case of a general grading", with "graded free Lie algebra whose homogeneous subspaces are of much smaller dimension", motivated by "composition and splitting methods, methods involving the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula" — [Munthe-Kaas & Owren (PDF mirror)](https://typeset.io/pdf/computations-in-a-free-lie-algebra-34cy1go7dw.pdf); [arXiv:math.NA/9904122](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math.NA/9904122).
- Witt's formula for the free Lie algebra on k generators: dim L_n = (1/n) Σ_{d|n} μ(d) k^{n/d}, "the number of inequivalent non-periodic colorings of a circular string of N beads with at most R colors" — [Bull. Aust. Math. Soc., "On Witt's dimension formula…"](https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/journals/bulletin-of-the-australian-mathematical-society/article/on-witts-dimension-formula-for-free-lie-algebras-and-a-theorem-of-klyachko/1E9387A845BAA2C3973E05F0D26539CB); [Kang & Kim, generalized Witt formula](https://wicri-demo.istex.fr/Wicri/Mathematiques/explor/BourbakiV1/Site/fr/Main/Exploration/bibRecord.php?hk=001A97). For k = 3 the first six values computed from the formula are 3, 3, 8, 18, 48, 116 (verified by hand in the search round; terms 312 and 810 for n = 7, 8 follow from the same formula but were not independently confirmed from a source).
- Polynomial Poisson algebras of pairwise 1/r² models: a paper on "polynomial Poisson algebras of observables for the classical Euler–Calogero–Moser models" (N particles on a line with pairwise 1/r² interactions) — [arXiv:hep-th/9404040](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-th/9404040); and a note that "polynomials in the relative coordinates and momenta do not form a closed finite-dimensional Lie algebra", requiring an infinite-dimensional extension "sometimes referred to as w∞" — [arXiv:hep-th/9611167](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-th/9611167). Neither reports a depth-graded dimension sequence; both concern symmetry algebras, not control-type generated algebras.
- Bosonic/Weyl-algebra side (quantum, but the same polynomial-Hamiltonian question): Bruschi, Xuereb, Zeier (J. Phys. A 2024; arXiv:2401.00069) study when Lie algebras generated by bosonic Hamiltonians are finite-dimensional, "tightly connected to ... the Weyl algebra", noting such algebras "can potentially be infinite dimensional" — [arXiv:2401.00069](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2401.00069); a 2025 follow-up classifies "finite-dimensional, non-abelian subalgebras of the single-mode skew-Hermitian Weyl algebra" — [arXiv:2511.06940](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06940); Karwowski & Vilela Mendes: "Results for controllability in infinite dimensions have been mostly negative, stating control cannot be achieved with a finite-dimensional control Lie algebra" — [Vilela Mendes PDF](https://label2.tecnico.ulisboa.pt/vilela/Papers/qinfinite.pdf). None reports a depth-wise dimension sequence.

### Inferences
- Your computation is a direct generalisation of McLachlan–Ryland/Murua: they take generators {T, V} (two generators, one grading), you take three pairwise Hamiltonians {H_12, H_13, H_23} (three generators). The same phenomena they document — strict sub-freeness from the quadratic-in-momentum structure, a graded dimension sequence, and an exponential growth rate ("algebraic entropy") — are the natural frame for your numbers. Compare your per-length sequence 3, 3, 8, 17, 44, 103, 272, 572 with the free Lie algebra on 3 generators 3, 3, 8, 18, 48, 116, 312, 810 (Witt): equality through length 3, first deficit (one relation) at length 4, growing deficits thereafter. (Inference from the Witt formula; the first deficit at length 4 is consistent with McLachlan–Ryland's observation that identities for mechanical systems appear in brackets of the form {V,{V,{V,T}}}, i.e. at length 4 — "consistent with", not "explained by", since your generators each contain kinetic terms.)
- An "algebraic entropy" lim (dim per length)^{1/n} for your algebra would be the direct analogue of their 1.8249…; your ratios 572/272 ≈ 2.10, 272/103 ≈ 2.64 have not converged, so no estimate is implied.
- The splitting-integrator connection is explicit in both McLachlan papers (number of order conditions at order n = dim of the degree-n graded piece), which ties your depth-graded sequence to the "Splitting integrator literature check" folder this note sits in.

### Gaps
- Could not read either McLachlan paper in full; the actual tables of c_n (graded dimensions) and the exact grading conventions (word length vs momentum degree vs bidegree) could not be extracted. Queries tried: "McLachlan 'Lie algebra of classical mechanics' ... dimensions graded free Lie algebra identities"; "McLachlan Ryland algebraic entropy ... dimension table". Recommend obtaining arXiv:1905.07554 (Tables) directly.
- No source at all for the Lie algebra generated by *several* pairwise Hamiltonians H_ij on N ≥ 3 bodies with depth-graded dimensions. Queries tried: "Poisson algebra generated by pairwise interaction Hamiltonians infinite dimensional Lie algebra polynomials"; "'Lie algebra' generated by kinetic energy and potential 'Poisson bracket' infinite-dimensional 'nested' Hamiltonian splitting integrator order conditions dimension"; "Lie algebra generated by polynomial Hamiltonians Poisson bracket controllability classical mechanics infinite-dimensional Rabitz". All negative for N-body pairwise sets.

## Key question 4 — Quantum many-body: "Lie algebra generated by two-body interactions" (nuclear/molecular dynamical symmetry; universality with two-body Hamiltonians); counting nested commutators of 2-local Hamiltonians

### Takeaway
In nuclear/molecular physics the relevant notion is the spectrum-generating / dynamical-symmetry algebra (a finite Lie algebra in which one- plus two-body Hamiltonians are expanded), which is a different question (which finite algebra contains H) from "what algebra do the two-body terms generate". The universality literature (Dodd–Nielsen–Bremner–Thew; Bremner et al.; Albertini–D'Alessandro) determines *which* closed algebra 2-body terms generate (su, so, sp), and the DLA classifications (Wiersema et al., Kökcü et al.) make this systematic by interaction graph; none counts nested commutators per depth.

### Cited Findings
- Spectrum-generating algebra definition: "an algebraic model is an expansion of the Hamiltonian and other operators in terms of elements of an algebra (often a Lie algebra, or a contraction of it). The algebra is called the spectrum generating algebra (SGA)" — [Encyclopedia of Mathematics](https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Spectrum_generating_algebra). Dynamical symmetry: "occurs if the hamiltonian is written in terms of Casimir operators of a set of nested algebras", with sufficient conditions on two-body interaction strengths for solvability — [Seniority in quantum many-body systems I, arXiv:1406.4094](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.4094). Elliott SU(3) and Wigner SU(4) as standard nuclear examples — [arXiv:2107.03831](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.03831).
- Universality: Dodd, Nielsen, Bremner, Thew — "an efficient algorithm to simulate any desired two-body Hamiltonian evolution using any fixed two-body entangling n-qubit Hamiltonian and local unitaries" — [arXiv:quant-ph/0106064](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0106064). Bremner et al., "Fungible dynamics: there are only two types of entangling multiple-qubit interactions": an odd Hamiltonian with local unitaries "generates either the simple Lie algebra so(2^n) or sp(2^n)" — [arXiv:quant-ph/0307148](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/quant-ph/0307148); extension identifying the only non-universal class as odd-Pauli-term Hamiltonians — [arXiv:quant-ph/0405115](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0405115).
- Parity quantum computing defines universality as "linear combinations of elements of the generator set as well as nested commutators of those elements fill it out", using the adjoint map expansion as the technical tool — [arXiv:2504.03556](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.03556).
- Graph-based many-body controllability: "controllability depends on two interaction graphs, one from the drift and one from the controlled dynamics, through the LARC" — [Controllability and accessibility on graphs for bilinear systems over Lie groups (abstract)](https://academicnewsletter.sufe.edu.cn/info/389810); Albertini–D'Alessandro link controllability of spin networks to connectedness of the interaction graph — [arXiv:quant-ph/0106115](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0106115v1). Infinite-dimensional many-body quantum control (bosonic lattices) — [arXiv:1308.4629](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.4629).

### Inferences
- "Two-body operators close into a finite Lie algebra" (dynamical symmetry) and "two-body generators generate a (possibly huge) algebra" (DLA/universality) are complementary; your classical computation belongs to the second camp. In qubit systems the second camp's answer is always finite, which is why nobody there tabulates depth; the classical polynomial setting is where the depth grading becomes the main invariant.

### Gaps
- No source found that "counts nested commutators of 2-local Hamiltonians" by depth. Queries tried: "universal quantum computation two-body Hamiltonians Lie algebra generated nested commutators counting"; "Lie algebra closure two-body interactions spectrum generating algebra dynamical symmetry ... closure commutators infinite". Negative.

## Consolidated verdict on "named home" (for the report writer)

1. **Named, closest, classical:** McLachlan–Ryland (2003) and McLachlan–Murua (2019), "the Lie algebra of classical mechanics" — graded Poisson algebra generated by {T, V}, dimensions per degree computed, compared with Witt/free counts, growth constant 1.8249…, explicit vanishing identities, direct link to splitting-method order conditions. Your object is the three-generator pairwise-Hamiltonian analogue; no one appears to have done it. (Depth-graded: YES.)
2. **Named, analogous, classical:** growth vector of a bracket-generating distribution (Chow–Rashevskii; Agrachev–Sachkov; Sachkov's free Carnot (2,3,5,8)). Depth-graded by definition, but finite and pointwise. (Depth-graded: YES; different object.)
3. **Named, analogous, quantum:** dynamical Lie algebra of a 2-local generator set (Larocca et al.; Ragone et al.; Wiersema et al.; Kökcü et al.; Aguilar et al.). Same construction, but the literature reports only closed dimension/scaling. (Depth-graded: NO in accessible text; appears implicitly as iteration count in `lie_closure`/`fastdla`.)
4. **Classical N-body controllability precedent:** Sarychev, "Controlling multiparticle system on a line" I & II — pairwise potentials, Lie-rank/accessibility, but switches external forces rather than interactions; no dimension sequences. (Depth-graded: NO.)
5. **Not found anywhere:** depth-graded dimension sequence of the Poisson algebra generated by {p_i²/2 + p_j²/2 + V(q_i − q_j)} over pairs (i,j) for N ≥ 3.
